newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt sees chance of metalworker wage deal.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt sees chance of metalworker wage deal.

text.p: The Italian government believes that the chances of a wage deal being struck between engineering and metalworkers and their employers have significantly improved, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Friday.

"The climate has changed in a positive sense. Today we have seen there is a will to reach the last lap," Treu told reporters after leaving a meeting between Prime Minister Romano Prodi and leaders of metalworker unions.
He said that the government had called a meeting in Rome for Monday between representatives of Confindustria, the employers' federation, and union leaders.
Unions and employers have been locked in a bitter dispute for many months over renewal of rolling wage contracts for the 1996-98 period.

Gabriele Albertini, the President of Federmeccanica, which groups engineering employers, said in Bologna on Friday that he thought the prospects for striking a non-inflationary deal had never been better.
"For the first time in 25 years, we have the opportunity to renew a contract in a non-inflationary way. Let's hope this objective can be reached in the coming days." Milan newsroom +392-66102321
